findings.message: A linked worktree that does not live under `.kata/worktrees/` — the shape `kata-cli worktree create --path /elsewhere` and a hand-run `git worktree add` produce — is not recognised by `worktreeContaining`, which is a pure `.kata/worktrees/<dir>` path test even though its docstring says it also recognises 'a git worktree listed by `git worktree list` (which is how a `--path` checkout appears)'. Because `worktreeContaining` returns undefined, `worktreeTaskId` returns undefined, `recordOwner` returns `ownerRoot: undefined`, and both `wikiDir` and `evidenceDir` keep a per-root copy inside the worktree via the `?? start` fallback — the exact defect this change removes, and the reason `worktreeOnlyRecords` (which does call `gitWorktreeList`) and `recordOwner` disagree for that shape. Under such a worktree the Wiki closure is still unsatisfiable, so AC-1's 'from inside a linked worktree' is not met. Reproduced by me on the frozen revision: X1, code 1.
findings.falsifier: Challenge X1: `test "$(node dist/cli.js wiki candidate --root <primary>)" = "$(node dist/cli.js wiki candidate --root <primary>-linked)"` exits 1 (reddens under the defect, green if the worktree resolved to its owner).
classInstances: src/core/layout.ts evidenceDir — same `recordOwner({ root: start, taskId: worktreeTaskId(start) })` and the same `?? start` fallback
src/core/layout.ts recordOwner — the undefined-worktreeRoot branch yields ownerRoot undefined
src/core/layout.ts resolveCodeRoot — the same `.kata/worktrees/`-only path test, so the docstring's claim that 'resolveCodeRoot recognised it' is also false
src/core/layout.ts worktreeContaining docstring versus body — a stated capability with no implementation

findings.message: `worktreeTaskId` returns the sorted-first task id it finds in the worktree's own `.kata/tasks/`, and `recordOwner` then walks only for that id. When the worktree holds a record directory for a task no non-worktree checkout holds (the 'stranded / worktree-only records' state this change itself handles via `worktreeOnlyRecords`/`recoverWorktreeRecords`), `findOwningCheckout` returns undefined and the task-less surfaces `wikiDir` and `evidenceDir` fall back into the worktree — a second store, under a directory `archive` deletes — while `recordsRoot(worktree, <the working task>)` still answers the owner. `worktreeTaskId`'s catch-comment ('any task id serves: the owner walk only has to reach the checkout that owns `.kata/worktrees/`, which does not depend on which task was asked') and the design doc's 'a worktree whose task has an owner never takes the fallback' are both false for this shape. Reproduced by me on the frozen revision: X2, code 1.
findings.falsifier: Challenge X2: a `.kata/worktrees/task-a` worktree carrying `.kata/tasks/other-task/judge.json` makes `wiki candidate --root <worktree>` read `<worktree>/.kata/wiki` instead of the primary's; the `test` exits 1. Equivalently, add the case to `tests/unit/record-ownership-answers-every-surface.test.ts` asserting `wikiDir(worktree) === join(recordOwner({root:worktree, taskId:held}).ownerRoot, '.kata', 'wiki')` when the worktree's first held task has no owner — it reddens.
classInstances: src/core/layout.ts evidenceDir — identical `worktreeTaskId`-driven fallback
src/core/layout.ts worktreeTaskId — `.sort()[0]` makes the answer depend on an unrelated directory the worktree happens to contain
src/wiki/store.ts readWikiRecordsWithIssues → this determines the candidate set every Wiki consumer sees

findings.message: AC-2's 'a registered candidate evaluates valid when asked from inside its linked worktree' is a corollary of C1, so it fails wherever C1's answer flips: from a `--path` worktree, or from a `.kata/worktrees/<id>` worktree holding a task id the owner does not hold, `evaluateWikiClosure(root, taskId)` reads the closure through `taskDir`/`recordsRoot` (owner) but the candidate set through `wikiDir` (the worktree's empty store), and answers `candidate_missing` for a candidate registered in the primary — with a remedy that reproduces the state. The selector only exercises the bare `.kata/worktrees/<id>` shape.
findings.falsifier: Extend the fixture of `tests/unit/wiki-closure-follows-its-owner.test.ts` so the worktree carries `.kata/tasks/<a-task-no-checkout-owns>/` and register a candidate in the primary, then ask `evaluateWikiClosure(worktree, 'wiki-task')`; it returns `{ valid: false, reason: 'candidate_missing' }` where the claim says `valid: true`.
classInstances: src/wiki/closure.ts evaluateWikiClosure — candidate set from `readWikiRecordsWithIssues(root)` → `wikiDir`
src/cli/wiki.ts `wiki candidate` / `wiki closure` — root is the workspace/code root, so the same flip is user-reachable

findings.message: `owningCheckoutOf` (src/core/layout.ts:787-795) answers a path-shaped worktree's owner from the path alone — 'the checkout above `.kata/worktrees/`' — and `recordOwner` (868-869) tries it first, before git, without checking that the named checkout holds the task or is not itself a linked worktree. For a worktree created inside a worktree the checkout above is the *outer linked worktree*, so the Wiki store, the evidence store and every record path resolve there. Reproduced by me: with a candidate registered in the primary, `wiki candidate --root <primary>` lists it and `wiki candidate --root <primary>/.kata/worktrees/outer/.kata/worktrees/inner` answers `[]`, while `git worktree list` run inside that inner checkout names the primary as `main` — git is never consulted. The shape is reachable through the product, not only by hand: `runWorktreeCommand` (src/cli/ops.ts:149) resolves `resolveWorkspaceRoot()`, which answers the worktree the command stands in (its `.git` is a marker), and `createWorktree` targets `join(worktreesDir(root), taskId)` (src/workflow/worktree.ts:94) — so `kata-cli worktree create` run from inside a linked worktree creates `<outer>/.kata/worktrees/<id>`. This contradicts `recordOwner`'s own decision (3), 'the owner is the nearest checkout that holds the task and is not a linked worktree', and C1's sentence that the primary and a linked worktree answer the same directory. It is a regression: before the first repair, a task-addressed `findOwningCheckout` answered the primary for this shape.
findings.falsifier: Challenge X3 (open, code 1): `test "$(node dist/cli.js wiki candidate --root <primary>)" = "$(node dist/cli.js wiki candidate --root <inner nested worktree>)"` exits 1. Unit form: `recordOwner({ root: <inner> }).ownerRoot` is expected to be the primary and is the outer linked worktree; `wikiDir(<inner>)` is expected to equal `wikiDir(<primary>)` and is not.
classInstances: wikiDir (1178) and evidenceDir (766): both stores move into the outer worktree
recordsRoot (610) / taskDir (644) and everything built on it (taskPath, currentStatePath, wikiClosurePath, revisionsDir, handoffDir)
worktreeOnlyRecords (459) / uniqueCopies: a worktree nested under a worktree is compared against the outer worktree instead of the repository root

recordOwner's docstring still says the walk 'continues upward from there, so a worktree nested inside another directory still resolves to the repository that owns it' — the walk it names no longer exists, and the sentence is false for this shape

a path-shaped worktree created inside this one by another repository (`git -C <other> worktree add <root>/.kata/worktrees/<dir>`): the owner is read off the path and git's `main` entry is never consulted

findings.message: The repair replaced a worktree caller's task-addressed branch (`findOwningCheckout`) with `worktreeOwnerOf`, which answers from the path or from git and never asks whether that checkout holds the task. So `ownerRoot` is *defined but wrong* for a task whose records exist only under a worktree — the stranded shape this repository maintains three mechanisms for (`worktreeOnlyRecords`, `uniqueCopies`, `recoverWorktreeRecords`/`worktree recover`). Reproduced by me: with `.kata/tasks/only-here/current-state.json` present only under `.kata/worktrees/wt`, `kata-cli status --change only-here` run from inside that worktree reads `<primary>/.kata/tasks/only-here/current-state.json` and fails with ENOENT — the reader looked in a checkout that has no state for the task. `recordsRoot`'s own paragraph at 608 ('When nothing else holds the task the worktree is still used, because an unreachable record is worse than a remote one') is dead for worktree callers, because the new branch always returns a value and the fallback at 618-631 never runs. Also a regression: before the first repair this shape resolved to the worktree. Consequences: `RecordOwnership.ownerRoot`, documented as 'The checkout holding this record', names a checkout with no `.kata/tasks/<id>`; `resolveWorkspaceRootForTask` (189) refuses stranded tasks from the only checkout holding them; and a writer through `taskDir` creates the record in the other checkout (one task with two record roots).
findings.falsifier: Challenge X4 (open, code 1): `status --change only-here` from inside the worktree holding the task's only records is expected to resolve to that worktree; it reads the primary and fails. Invariant to assert: `ownerRoot !== undefined` implies `readdirSync(join(ownerRoot, '.kata', 'tasks', taskId))` succeeds.
classInstances: resolveWorkspaceRootForTask (189): every stranded task is refused from the only checkout holding it
currentStatePath (654) -> the local status command: reads a path in a checkout with no state for the task
wikiClosurePath (687) and evaluateWikiClosure: a closure recorded before the repair lives with the worktree and is now read from the primary
taskDir as a writer's target (writeWikiClosure's mkdir, mutateTaskArtefact's lock path): new records materialise in a checkout that does not hold the task
recordsRoot (610): the documented fallback is unreachable for worktree callers, so the paragraph and the code disagree

findings.message: `worktreeOwnerOf`'s docstring (798-803) says a worktree whose owner neither source can name 'stays `undefined`, which the callers read as "no owner" rather than as "here"' — but the callers cannot: `wikiDir` (1183-1184) and `evidenceDir` (777-778) receive only `ownerRoot` and read `undefined` as `join(kataDir(start), …)`, i.e. 'here', because the `worktreeRoot` that would distinguish 'a worktree I could not name' from 'not a worktree at all' is discarded. Reproduced by me: a git-listed worktree whose `.git` file exists but whose gitdir is gone (`.git` rewritten to `gitdir: /nonexistent/...`) makes git exit 128, `gitWorktreeList` return `[]`, the gate at 923-936 pass, and `wiki candidate --root <that worktree>` answer `[]` while the primary lists the candidate — the fail-open direction this change removes. I could not reproduce the round's original construction (removing `.git/worktrees/<name>`): git still answered there, naming the primary as `main`, and the candidate list matched the primary.
findings.falsifier: Challenge X5 (open, code 1): with `.git` rewritten to a nonexistent gitdir, the candidate list from the primary and from the worktree differ. The distinction the callers need — `worktreeRoot !== undefined && ownerRoot === undefined` — is available from `recordOwner` and unused by either store.
classInstances: evidenceDir (766): the same `?? start` fallback for the evidence store
recordsRoot (610): the same fallback direction
the fail-open reading of `undefined` is the exact direction this change was written to remove, so leaving it in the one case its own docstring names is the residual

findings.message: Nested worktrees under an outside-path linked worktree resolve the Wiki store to the outer linked checkout, not the primary owner. `owningCheckoutOf` only recognizes an outer linked checkout via the `.kata/worktrees` path shape.
findings.falsifier: Create a linked worktree at an outside path, then create its child at <outer>/.kata/worktrees/inner. `wikiDir(inner)` resolves to <outer>/.kata/wiki, while `wikiDir(primary)` resolves to <primary>/.kata/wiki.

custom-path-worktree
owner-resolution

findings.message: The same outside-path nested-worktree shape makes Wiki closure read candidates from the outer linked checkout. A candidate registered in the primary store is therefore reported `candidate_missing` from the inner worktree.
findings.falsifier: Register a candidate in the primary checkout, then evaluate a captured closure from an inner worktree at <outside-outer>/.kata/worktrees/inner. `wikiDir(inner)` selects <outside-outer>/.kata/wiki, where the candidate is absent, so closure evaluation fails closed with `candidate_missing`.
classInstances: wiki-closure
nested-worktree
custom-path-worktree

findings.message: writeWikiRecord and updateWikiRecord resolve an owner-owned Wiki file but derive withRepositoryArtefactLock from the caller root. A primary checkout and a linked-worktree caller therefore write the same file under different lock directories.
findings.impact: Concurrent updates can each read the prior bytes and atomically overwrite the other update; the file remains valid JSON while one state transition is silently lost.

src/wiki/store.ts:74 updateWikiRecord
